- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after a recent spike or recovery.
- Model overestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, particularly when true prices are rising sharply.
- Model exhibits lag in capturing sudden price spikes; forecasts often peak too early or too late relative to true price movements.
- Model shows mean reversion bias: tends to forecast prices back toward historical averages too aggressively, missing sustained upward trends.
- Model underreacts to recent high prices; fails to anticipate continuation or acceleration of upward momentum.
- Model overreacts to minor price corrections or volatility, leading to premature downward adjustments.
- Model tends to overfit short-term noise, especially in the first 10 days, while underfitting longer-term trends.
- Model often fails to account for policy or market event-driven price jumps, leading to persistent underestimation in the 15–30 day window.
